Moreover, the administrator of lodgement—that is, myself—has won no credit for his place of giving lodgement for this matter. Let every one see your good sense and admire you.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: "Moreover, if there is any affair or consideration between you and any one, that other person will certainly be present to your discomfiture; do not spite your own self. For when death comes peacefully and naturally, people console themselves, for they call it 'the lot of mankind', since it is the fate of every one; but in this place where you are now sentence is passed upon murderers and temple robbers and violators of graves and debauchees and adulterers and villains—no respectable person is brought out from here and destroyed. But if there is any one who has flouted the law, it is evident to every one that what has betrayed such a person is not wisdom, but an insanity of conceit; just as robbers are reckless of death for robbery's sake.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: "Now I have been lenient with you so far, so that you may see sense and live a life of liberty like any free man.... Colluthus, why don't you speak to me when I am speaking to you?"
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said, "It is not fitting for me to make a long speech before a governor."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Do sacrifice, Colluthus!"
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said, "I will not sacrifice."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Indeed you have not obeyed me and sacrificed to the gods about whom the Emperor has written to me. I shall consume your body by fire. But this shall not happen yet, in case you wish to consider with yourself."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint answered, "I have already considered with myself before I came here to you."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The advocates said to him, "Grant him a few days, if you please." Arianus said to the advocates, "He looks to me as if he wants to, and has changed his mind." The governor said to him, "Do you want to wait a few days, to think the matter over? For I can see it in your face—it shows me that you want to be saved."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint made no answer at all...
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Are you ashamed to admit it?"
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said to him, "A word is enough to the wise."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor had the fire laid before the blessed Colluthus. The governor said to them, "Stop, don't do him any harm yet."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: Then the governor turned to the holy Colluthus and said to him, "Be sensible now, and do as you are told. There was Apollonius, the bishop of Siout; his people were most understanding about him, and took a dignified view of his prudence, since he did not wish to be disobedient, or to be brought to court and hear all this rigmarole, but he proceeded of his own accord into the temple and sacrificed in full view of every one, with the vessels of libation in his hand, standing there and offering up sacrifice; he is not at all ashamed, and every one honours him.... Well now, speak to me, Colluthus, and you shall be in especial honour....
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: Then there was Plutarchus, the bishop of Sbeht; this man for the excellence of his wisdom is worthy of all respect. He was prudent and reverenced the Emperor's gods, and offered up sacrifice to them; and look at him now! He is alive, with every one who sacrificed with him, and is bishop over them. As for you, Colluthus, it is a governor who is pleading with you, and advising you! The governorship has humbled itself for you. Let it be enough to have done what you have in the matter of the books, when you were persuaded by your God and did not burn them.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: "There was a man here today on a charge of murder. That man wants to live; but as for you, Colluthus, something evil possesses you, to make you destroy yourself with murderers! Don't you see the beauty of this pleasant weather? There will be no pleasure to come your way if you kill your own self. But listen to me and you will be saved."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to him, "The death which is coming to me is more pleasant than the life which you would give me."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "So you do not realize that I have authority to chastise you? Come now, use your reason like a sensible man, and listen to me."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to him, "Whoever listens to you will bring his own death upon himself. But I will not forsake my Lord Jesus Christ."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Look at all these people with their tears streaming down as they see you standing on the tribunal—and you have shown no pity on your own self, but you are disobedient. Now, listen to me and sacrifice, and you shall live."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said to him, "This life is indeed no life to me, but death."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: And straightway he ordered him to be set up on the rack.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "You do not need any one to ask you—do you want me to grant you some more days?"
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: Besamon the advocate said, "Yes, that is his wish."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "What do you want? Say, and I will do it for you."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: Jeremias the chief advocate said, "My lord, this is indeed what he wishes—that you should bear with him for a few days more; for his silence tells us this; (we know) from his demeanour."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said, "Colluthus, why don't you speak? Which do you want me to do—to sentence you, or to be lenient with you?"
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The righteous man said to him, "Do what you like."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Thus far till now I have been lenient with you. If you for your part will only be lenient with yourself, then I shall be all the more pleased."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said to him, "Your kindness constrains me to say a word more."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Now I have begun to hear a good word from you. For this kind of speech tells me that you want me to leave you for a few more days."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to the governor, "What are these words of comfort which you are saying? I will no longer listen to you and be misled so as to forsake my God; but I am rather confirmed in His Faith. And I am ready to bear anything for the sake of His holy Name; for the torments of this world are nothing, but the torments of God are great, and eternal, and there is none who shall be able to hide in His presence."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor ordered a great stone to be hung upon his neck. The governor said to him, "Colluthus, do not say a word to me about anything but the matter which we are hoping for—that you will obey the law of the Emperors." But the saint spoke no word at all.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Think scorn of this vain glory which will be of no profit to you! Turn now, man, and take for yourself a glory worthy of respect."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said to him, "The glory of my Lord Jesus Christ will preserve me for ever."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "We are not demanding from you a contest of words with us, but we are demanding from you an urgent matter—that you should be persuaded by us and sacrifice to the gods. Well, then, consider with yourself."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to him, "Do not detain me any more."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "You have been ordered to be wise and not show contempt of the court."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to him, "I have been wise all the time; and I came here in pursuit of the wisdom of my Lord Jesus Christ."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to the members of the entourage, "There, you see; I have used every possible means with him in the hope of saving him; and you see how he would not listen and be saved. I am just not going to tolerate him for another single moment."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The members of the entourage said, "Sentence him; he deserves to die, for he has dared to mislead us, and he made us a promise and broke it, when he mocked us and did not sacrifice."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said to them, "I said no word which it was not proper to say."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor said to him, "Sacrifice and be sensible."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The saint said to him, "I will not sacrifice, neither will I listen to your stupid arguments."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The governor was angry, and said to him, "If you will not sacrifice, hear your sentence, which you have earned: I order you to be burned alive."
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: The holy Colluthus said, "I thank You, my Lord Jesus Christ, that I have been deemed worthy of Your grace, to die for the sake of Your holy Name." And he was taken out to be burned.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: Now that day was the twenty-fourth of the month Pashons, and the holy Colluthus fulfilled his martyrdom, and his soul was taken up to heaven in glory, and he made festival with the angels, and all the saints rejoiced with him through the grace and compassion of our Lord Jesus Christ; with whom is the glory of the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever, Amen.
paragraphs.author: Martyrdom of Colluthus

paragraphs.text: For this present, momentary, and light tribulation is not spoken of for all, but for Paul and for those who are like him: because they have the perfect charity of God in Christ Jesus poured out in their heart through the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.author: Origen of Alexandria
paragraphs.work: COMMENTARY ON THE SONG OF SONGS, PROLOGUE

paragraphs.text: You may learn this, too, from the following passage, where the apostle says: "For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for as a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; while we look not at the things which are seen," that is, our sufferings, "but at the things which are not seen," that is, our rewards: "for the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal." For the afflictions and injuries wherewith the outward man is worn away, he affirms to be only worthy of being despised by us, as being light and temporary; preferring those eternal recompenses which are also invisible, and that "weight of glory" which will be a counterpoise for the labours in the endurance of which the flesh here suffers decay.
paragraphs.author: Tertullian
paragraphs.work: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

paragraphs.text: Paul is saying that people who long for heavenly things despise the things of this world, because in comparison with what they want, these things are nothing.
paragraphs.author: Ambrosiaster

paragraphs.text: If you seek temporal things, you pray publicly and with your door open. If you ask for eternal things, your prayer is secret because you long to receive not the things which are seen but those which are not seen.
paragraphs.author: Caesarius of Arles

paragraphs.text: Head-dresses and varieties of head-dresses, and elaborate braidings, and infinite modes of dressing the hair, and costly specimens of mirrors, in which they arrange their costume,-hunting after those that, like silly children, are crazy about their figures,-are characteristic of women who have lost all sense of shame. If any one were to call these courtesans, he would make no mistake, for they turn their faces into masks. But us the Word enjoins "to look not on the things that are seen, but the things that are not seen; for the things that are seen are temporal, but the things that are not seen are eternal."
paragraphs.author: Clement of Alexandria

paragraphs.text: More grievous and painful is this persecution, which arises from within, which is ever with a man, and which the persecuted cannot escape; for he carries the enemy about everywhere in himself. Thus also burning which attacks from without works trial, but that from within produces death. War also made on one is easily put an end to, but that which is in the soul continues till death.
paragraphs.author: Clement of Alexandria
paragraphs.work: Who is the Rich Man that Shall Be Saved?

paragraphs.text: With such persecution, if you have worldly wealth, if you have brothers allied by blood and other pledges, abandon the whole wealth of these which leads to evil; procure peace for yourself, free yourself from protracted persecutions; turn from them to the Gospel; choose before all the Saviour and Advocate and Paraclete of your soul, the Prince of life. "For the things which are seen are temporary; but the things which are not seen are eternal." And in the present time are things evanescent and insecure, but in that to come is eternal life.
paragraphs.author: Clement of Alexandria
paragraphs.work: Who is the Rich Man that Shall Be Saved?

paragraphs.text: Ye have never envied any one; ye have taught others. Now I desire that those things may be confirmed [by your conduct], which in your instructions ye enjoin [on others]. Only request in my behalf both inward and outward strength, that I may not only speak, but [truly] will; and that I may not merely be called a Christian, but really be found to be one. For if I be truly found [a Christian], I may also be called one, and be then deemed faithful, when I shall no longer appear to the world. Nothing visible is eternal. "For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal." For our God, Jesus Christ, now that He is with the Father, is all the more revealed [in His glory]. Christianity is not a thing of silence only, but also of [manifest] greatness.
paragraphs.author: Ignatius of Antioch
paragraphs.work: Epistle of Ignatius to the Romans

paragraphs.text: Consider, dearly beloved, that life's troubles, even if distressing, are still of short duration, whereas the good things that will come to us in the next life are eternal and everlasting. "What we see is passing," Scripture says, "but what is not seen is everlasting." Accordingly, let us endure what is passing without complaint and not desist from virtue's struggle so that we may enjoy the good things that are eternal and last forever.
paragraphs.author: John Chrysostom

paragraphs.text: Far from being surprised or troubled, let us endure developments with complete fortitude and endurance, having regard not to the distress but to the gain accruing to us from it. This transaction, you see, is spiritual. People intent on making money and being involved in a transaction of this life would succeed in increasing their wealth in no other way than by being exposed to great danger on land and at sea (they must, after all, put up with the onset of brigands and wiles of pirates), and yet they are ready to accept everything with great enthusiasm, having no sense of hardship through the expectation of gain. In just the same way must we keep our mind on the wealth and spiritual riches accruing to us from this. We must rejoice and be glad, considering not what can be seen but what cannot be seen, as Paul's exhortation goes, "not considering what can be seen."
paragraphs.author: John Chrysostom

paragraphs.text: And, to show you that he was as it were in solitude, and so looked upon the things present, hear himself saying, "While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen." What sayest thou? Answer me. And yet what thou sayest is the contrary; thou seest the things invisible, and the visible thou seest not. Such eyes as thou hadst gotten, such are the eyes which are given by Christ: for as these bodily eyes see indeed the things that are seen, but things unseen they see not: so those heavenly eyes do the contrary: no one that beholds the invisible things, beholds the visible: no one beholding the things seen, beholds the invisible. Or is not this the case with us also? For when having turned our mind inwards we think of any of the unseen things, our views become raised above the things on earth.
paragraphs.author: John Chrysostom

paragraphs.text: "For the things that are seen are temporal." Therefore the afflictions are so too. "But the things that are not seen are eternal." Therefore the crowns are so also. And he said not the afflictions are so, but "the things that are seen;" all of them, whether punishment or rest, so that we should be neither puffed up by the one nor overborne by the other. And therefore when speaking of the things to come, he said not the kingdom is eternal; but, "the things which are not seen are eternal," whether they be a kingdom, or again punishment; so as both to alarm by the one and to encourage by the other.
paragraphs.author: John Chrysostom

paragraphs.text: Since then "the things that are seen are temporal, but the things that are not seen are eternal," let us look to them. For what excuse even can we have, if we choose the temporal instead of the eternal? For even if the present be pleasurable, yet it is not abiding; whilst the woe it entails is abiding and irremissible.
paragraphs.author: John Chrysostom

paragraphs.text: Do thou then, O disciple, make use of faith in its fair order, and turn it not into error; and believe by it in God and in His promises, and believe not in the world and in its delights therewith. Everything which is seen is temporal, and everything which is unseen is eternal, even as Paul also taught; believe then in God, and hope that everlasting blessing will be given to thee by Him, and let faith be the beginning of the way of thy instruction. If thou believest not in these things which are invisible thou canst not forsake the things which are visible; and if thou believest not that the promise of Christ is sure and also in the blessings which were promised by Him to all those who should go forth after His Gospel, thou wilt not forsake that of which thou hast possession, and wilt not run after the good things which He promised to thee.
paragraphs.author: Philoxenus of Mabbug

paragraphs.text: And Paul revealed unto us the greatness of this exchange in one little word, and shewed us how inferior are the things which we have, and how great are those of God in one short verse, saying, "The things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are unseen are eternal." Who then would not exchange the things of time for those of eternity, except ourselves, and fools like unto us?
paragraphs.author: Philoxenus of Mabbug
